key_findings: 21 frontend business types have no training examples.
8 frontend industries have no training examples.
All app-only business type scenarios produced the same prediction — likely ignored by the model.
Changing only business_type/industry with fixed energy inputs did not change predictions at all.
Highest mean absolute error cluster: Factory (MAE ~₦1,739,007).
19 of top 20 worst errors are Factory businesses.
What-If sample sweep: 2/3 profiles show lower predicted cost at max generator reduction.
What-If sample sweep: 1/3 profiles have monotonic non-increasing predictions.
Population What-If: 82.9% direction-sensible at max reduction across 750 records.
Population What-If: 4.3% of records show flat predictions across all reduction levels.
Evidence-based generator dependency floor for reliable What-If direction: 5.0% (82.0% direction-sensible, n=557).
Dominant model driver: maintenance_cost; business identity features = 0.0% importance.
The model is primarily driven by current-month energy spend and usage signals. Industry and business_type labels contribute very little relative to energy inputs.
Highest target correlation on eval split: total_energy_cost (r=0.9535).
Lowest R² by business_type: School (0.6416); highest: Hotel (0.8773).

interpretation_notes: If app_only scenarios share one prediction, unknown categories are likely ignored by one-hot encoding.
If trained scenarios differ, business_type/industry affect predictions within training coverage.
Decoupled pairs simulate user-selected mismatches not present in synthetic training data.
Sensible direction means max-reduction scenario predicts lower cost than baseline.
Monotonic non-increasing means each step down in generator use does not raise the forecast.
What-If does not model grid replacement or operational constraints — treat as scenario estimates.
Direction sensible = predicted cost at 40% reduction is not higher than baseline.
Flat response = all five scenario predictions are within ₦1 of each other.
Use dependency buckets and empirical thresholds to set product guardrails with evidence.

whatif_recommended_minimum_generator_dep.note: Lowest tested threshold where at least 70% of records show non-increasing predicted cost at max generator reduction.

feature_importance.product_interpretation: The model is primarily driven by current-month energy spend and usage signals. Industry and business_type labels contribute very little relative to energy inputs.
interpretation_notes: Importances are aggregated across one-hot encoded categorical columns.
High total_energy_cost importance indicates autoregressive cost forecasting, not industry optimization.

leakage_sanity.product_interpretation: Features represent current-month observations and static business attributes forecasting next month's total energy cost. High R² is primarily driven by autoregressive cost persistence, not same-month leakage.
interpretation_notes: Medium-risk features derive from current-month total_energy_cost but remain temporally valid inputs.
Verify product copy describes next-month forecasting from current observed data.
GES and other post-hoc scores are excluded from the model contract.
